summary.title: DVAO: Dynamic Variance-adaptive Advantage Optimization for Multi-reward Reinforcement Learning

details: Multi-reward GRPO for LLMs is usually handled by scalarization: linearly combining raw rewards (Reward Combination) or combining separately normalized advantages (Advantage Combination).

Reward Combination yields advantages with larger squared magnitude (erratic gradients / instability); Advantage Combination uses static hand-tuned weights and normalizes each objective in isolation, ignoring cross-objective correlation.

DVAO: replaces the fixed convex weights w_k in advantage combination with variance-adaptive weights w̃_k = w_k·σ_k / Σ_l w_l·σ_l, where σ_k is the within-rollout-group standard deviation of reward k, so A_DVAO = (Σ_k w_k σ_k A_k)/(Σ_l w_l σ_l).

Effect: up-weights high-variance (informative) objectives, suppresses low-variance ones, fully data-driven with no extra hyperparameters; claimed to bound advantage magnitude and induce implicit cross-objective regularization.
Proposition 1: mean squared advantage of reward combination (=1 by normalization) ≥ that of advantage combination (=1 − 2Σ_{k<l}w_k w_l(1−ρ̂_kl)), equality iff all pairwise sample correlations are 1.
Proposition 2: pointwise |A_DVAO| ≤ |A_sum|, proved via Cauchy–Schwarz giving σ_sum ≤ Σ_k w_k σ_k; equality iff all reward pairs perfectly positively correlated.

Proposition 3: sensitivity ∂A/∂r_k for advantage combination depends on isolated (A_k)^2, while for DVAO it depends on the cross term A_DVAO·A_k, interpreted as cross-objective variance-aware regularization.
Assumptions: rewards r_k ∈ [0,1], convex weights summing to 1, group-normalized advantages, clipping/KL terms omitted for analysis.
Math reasoning: trained on DAPO-Math-17k with two objectives, accuracy reward and binary length reward (output within 4,000 tokens).
Tool use: trained on the ToolRL mixture (2k ToolACE + 1k Hammer + 1k xLAM) with accuracy (tool-call correctness) and binary format-compliance reward.
Unless stated otherwise all reward weights are equal, so all methods share the same initialization.
Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base for math; Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct for tool use.
Math benchmarks: AIME-2024/2025, MATH500, OlympiadBench, AMC23 (avg@16, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95); tool use: BFCL-v4.
verl framework, AdamW, constant LR 1e-6, prompt batch 128, G=16 rollouts, 500 training steps, max 8,192 generated tokens, 8×H20 GPUs.
Single-reward GRPO (accuracy only), Reward Combination (RC), Advantage Combination (AC), and GDPO (AC with batch-wise advantage normalization).
Pareto-frontier sweep over accuracy weight w1 ∈ {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9} with w2 = 1−w1 for both tasks.
Training-dynamics tracking of mean and std of accuracy and length rewards plus average response length (moving average window 15).

key_findings.finding: DVAO provably keeps advantage magnitudes no larger than raw reward combination while, unlike static advantage combination, coupling each objective's gradient sensitivity to overall multi-objective performance.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 2 shows |A_DVAO| ≤ |A_sum| pointwise (from σ_sum ≤ Σ_k w_k σ_k via Cauchy–Schwarz, equality only under perfect positive reward correlation); Proposition 3 derives ∂A_DVAO/∂r_k ∝ (1 − 1/G − A_DVAO·A_k/G) versus ∂A/∂r_k ∝ (1 − 1/G − (A_k)^2/G) for advantage combination.

key_findings.finding: Reward combination is inherently more gradient-explosive than advantage combination, formalizing a previously informal preference.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 1: group-mean squared advantage equals 1 for reward combination but 1 − 2Σ_{k<l}w_k w_l(1−ρ̂_kl) ≤ 1 for advantage combination, with equality only when all objectives are perfectly correlated within the group.

key_findings.finding: DVAO is the only method that simultaneously attains the best accuracy and near-perfect length/format compliance across both tasks and both model scales.
key_findings.evidence: Reported main results on math (Qwen3-4B/8B-Base) and tool use (Qwen2.5-3B/7B-Instruct): RC and AC trade accuracy for length compliance, GDPO gets near-perfect length compliance with the lowest accuracy, GRPO shows near-zero tool-use format compliance, and AC at 7B falls below the base model in accuracy; all methods use identical equal-weight initialization.

key_findings.finding: DVAO dominates the accuracy-versus-compliance Pareto frontier over the whole weight sweep, so its gain comes from adaptivity rather than a lucky weight choice.
key_findings.evidence: Sweeping w1 ∈ {0.1,...,0.9} on Qwen3-4B-Base math and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct tool use, DVAO occupies the upper-right region while RC saturates, AC is unstable, and GDPO fluctuates incoherently; the frontier shift is largest on the harder math task.

key_findings.finding: Variance-adaptive weighting empirically stabilizes training, producing higher mean rewards with sharply collapsing reward variance.
key_findings.evidence: Training-dynamics curves on Qwen3-4B/8B-Base show DVAO's accuracy reward above all baselines at every step with the lowest final accuracy-reward std (AC highest), length reward closest to 1.0 with std approaching near-zero on 8B, and the fastest growth in average response length from ~800 tokens without runaway exploration.
